title: Transfer of criminal cases - grounds courts accept
p1:
A criminal case can be transferred to another court — but not simply because one side feels uncomfortable.

Many people assume a transfer is granted whenever a party claims unfairness. The reality is that courts look for genuine reasons, not just allegations.
p2:
A surprising point: even a serious fear of bias may not be enough unless there are facts supporting that fear.

Courts usually consider factors like a real possibility of an unfair trial, threats to safety, extreme inconvenience for parties or witnesses, or circumstances that affect public confidence in the justice process.
p3:
Transfer powers exist to protect the fairness of the trial, not to provide a strategic advantage to either side.

For example, if witnesses cannot safely appear in one location or the accused cannot reasonably receive a fair hearing there, a higher court may consider moving the case.

The key takeaway: courts balance convenience with justice. A transfer is about protecting a fair process, not choosing a more favourable forum.
conclusion: Do you think courts should make it easier to transfer criminal cases when a party claims fear of an unfair trial?
